LPG traders call off strike after BERC promises to hear demands

quotes.text: LPG traders have withdrawn their planned two-day shutdown after securing talks with the energy regulator over seven demands, including higher commissions and an end to alleged harassment.
Association President Md Selim Khan told bdnews24.com the BERC chairman assured them at a 3pm meeting that their demands would be heard at a public hearing on Oct 29.
In a letter to BERC, the association said it costs Tk 50 to transport a cylinder from a company to a distributor's warehouse.
Loading, unloading and delivering it to retailers costs another Tk 35, while employee salaries, warehouse rent and other expenses amount to Tk 25.
Taking these costs into account and adding a Tk 40 profit margin, the association has demanded a commission of Tk 150 per cylinder.
The association's key demand is that distributors' commission on each LPG cylinder be raised to Tk 150 or set at 7 percent of the retail price.

Biological and technical spatial variation in ...

quotes.text: Spatial transcriptomics technologies enable the identification of spatially variable genes that can shed light on tissue structure and function. However, spatial variability of gene expression can be due not only to biological function but also technical artifact. We develop a model for spatially variable capture that forms part of a bursty transcription model, allowing us to distinguish biological variability from spatially variable technical noise. Our approach is implemented in a program called stipple, which we demonstrate can be useful for identifying and interpreting spatial gene expression variation from spatial transcriptomics assays.

12kg LPG cylinder price rises by Tk252 to Tk1,837 | The Business Standard

quotes.text: The price of a 12kg liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) cylinder has been increased by Tk252, taking the price to Tk1,837.

According to a BERC press notification issued today, the regulator calculated the October price based on Saudi Aramco's Contract Price (CP) for propane and butane, which stood at $680 and $730 per tonne respectively.
The price of private LPG at the retail level has been set at Tk153.06 per kg, including VAT. Accordingly, the price of a 12kg LPG cylinder has been fixed at Tk1,837, including VAT.

sources.title: Bangladesh's consumers still pay inflated LPG prices as cylinders remain scarce

quotes.text: On Wednesday, a resident of Paikpara in Mirpur said a retailer demanded Tk 2,400 for a cylinder, claiming his purchase cost was Tk 2,300.

LOAB President Mohammad Amirul Haque denied that distributors were being charged above the official rate, saying transactions were conducted through banks and cylinders supplied against bank receipts.

The association estimated per-cylinder costs at Tk 50 for transport to distributors’ warehouses, Tk 35 for loading, unloading and delivery to retailers, and Tk 25 for staff, rent, electricity, licence fees and other expenses. Including Tk 40 in distributor profit, it put the total at Tk 150.
Customers can exchange an empty cylinder for a full one from the same company, he said. Switching brands, however, means buying both a cylinder and its gas.
The country imported 156,000 tonnes in September, close to August’s 158,000 tonnes, which the association considers enough to meet demand.

sources.title: LPG source

quotes.text: In the first week of this month, the Bangladesh Energy Regulatory Commission (BERC) raised the official price of a 12kg cylinder by Tk 252, from Tk 1,585 to Tk 1,837. But consumers in major cities are paying up to Tk 2,500 a cylinder, well above the government rate.
Abu Sayed said only around 10 of Bangladesh’s 23 LPG operators imported the fuel in the previous month, leaving much of the country’s storage capacity unused.

Stevan Matheendra De Zoysa, chief operating officer of Omera LPG, said only six to eight of the country’s 27-28 registered operators have imported cargoes in recent months because geopolitical disruptions have made supplies harder to secure.

The shortage of liquefied natural gas (LNG) has also increased demand for LPG in industry recently, with consumption rising from around 15,000-16,000 tonnes a few months ago to 30,000-32,000 tonnes, Zoysa said.

He questioned whether the margins set for distributors and retailers, at Tk 50 and Tk 100 respectively for a 12kg cylinder, are sufficient to cover their operating costs. However, he said this does not justify charging consumers above the approved price.

BERC sets public hearing on LPG prices, bottling costs, dealer commissions

quotes.text: The Bangladesh Energy Regulatory Commission (BERC) will hold a public hearing on Oct 29 on proposals to revise government and private-sector liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) prices, bottling costs and commissions for distributors and retailers.
Interested individuals and organisations must submit written opinions to BERC by Oct 27.
Those wishing to attend must register by the same deadline.
Registered participants can present relevant data, calculations and documents. The proposals are available from BERC’s office and website.
